AboutBody: Blazma Sandbox analyzes suspicious files in an isolated environment and turns raw activity into an explainable report.
AboutFonts: Fonts: IBM Plex Sans Arabic and IBM Plex Mono (SIL Open Font License).
AboutPurpose: Built for defense, analysis and authorized security research. A high score describes behavior; it does not by itself prove a file is malicious.
AgentMissing: Blazma.Agent.exe was not found. Build or reinstall it.
AgentPresent: The monitoring agent is installed and talks to Blazma only through signed files.
AiFailed: The AI answer is not available
AiThinking: The local AI model is writing an explanation…
AskIntro: Answers come only from this report's recorded data. Each answer says whether it is an observed fact or a rule-based inference.
CancelAnalysisBody: The sandbox will be closed and destroyed. Events collected so far are kept in History.
ClearHistoryBody: Every stored analysis and its events will be deleted from this computer.
CollectDroppedHelp: Files the program creates are copied out and analyzed. They are stored without their name or extension so they cannot be opened by accident.
CommunityBody: Optional sharing of hash, behavior summary and indicators (never the file). Off until you enable it, and community votes will never decide a verdict on their own.
CompareHelp: For example version 1.2 against version 1.3 of the same installer: see which processes, connections, persistence and files are new.
DeleteBody: {0} and all its events will be removed from this computer.
DemoReportBanner: DEMO DATA: this analysis used synthetic events. No real file was run.
DemoSampleBanner: Demo sample: these details are synthetic and the analysis will use generated data. No file will run.
DropSafety: The file is inspected without being run, then executed only inside an isolated, disposable Windows Sandbox.
DropTitle: Drop a file here to analyze
DumpMemoryHelp: Looks for hidden program code in the memory of the analyzed processes (unpacked or injected code).
HistorySearch: Search by file name or hash
HistorySubtitle: Every analysis stays on this computer. Search, sort, export, compare or delete.
HostProtectionDetail: Samples never run on this computer. Static analysis runs in a separate helper process.
HowAnsweredBody: Ask Blazma reads the structured report (events, findings, chains), never the file itself, and never invents data. If something was not observed, it says so.
IndicatorsNote: Indicators are graded only by evidence. Nothing is labelled malicious without a finding that supports it.
IntegrityDetail: Version {0}. Development builds are not code-signed.
IntelSubtitle: Intelligence that stays on this computer: your watchlist and detection rules.
InteractiveModeHelp: You use the sandbox window yourself (click through installers, open files). The run does not stop early and you can extend it.
IsoChannel: Output is parsed strictly, size-limited, signed, and never executed
IsoDisposable: The sandbox is destroyed after every analysis
IsoFolders: Only two shared folders: input read-only, output write-only for results
IsoNetwork: Networking disabled unless you allow it for one analysis
IsolationNotReady: Windows Sandbox is not available on this system. Real analyses are disabled; the demo still works.
IsolationReady: Windows Sandbox is available. Each analysis runs in a fresh, disposable instance.
KeySaved: A key is saved (encrypted for your Windows account).
LocalAiBody: A local AI model for summaries and free-form questions is planned. It will be optional and will run on this computer only.
MonitoringInterruptedBanner: Monitoring was interrupted before the analysis ended. Results may be incomplete.
NetOffHelp: Nothing answers. Lookups are still recorded.
NetRealHelp: The program can reach the internet. Use only when you understand the risk.
NetSimulatedHelp: No real network. Addresses the program looks up are answered inside the sandbox, so you see where it tries to connect and what it sends.
NetworkConsent: I understand and want to allow network access for this analysis
NetworkMetadataNote: Blazma records connection metadata only (who connected where, when). It does not intercept or decrypt traffic.
NetworkPolicyDetail: Off by default. Can be enabled per analysis after an explicit warning.
NetworkWarning: Allowing internet access reduces isolation: the program could download more code or send data out. Use only when you understand the risk.
NewAnalysisSubtitle: Review the file and choose how to analyze it. Nothing runs until you press Start.
NoAnalysesYet: No analyses yet. Drop a file above or try the demo analysis.
NoFileSelectedBody: Choose a file or drop one on the dashboard.
NoFindings: No detection rule matched the observed behavior.
NoPersistence: No persistence was observed. The program did not configure itself to run again later.
NoSnapshot: No before/after snapshot was taken for this analysis.
NoiseNote: {0} background events from Windows itself were hidden (noise filter).
NotRunnable: Blazma can inspect this file, but cannot run this type of file in the sandbox.
OpenReportFirst: Open a report to export it
PaletteHint: ↑↓ to move · Enter to run · Esc to close
PdfPlanned: PDF export is planned. HTML and JSON are available now.
PointsToDropped: Points to a file created during the analysis
PrivacyDetail: Local-first: no uploads, no hash lookups, no telemetry.
RawNote: Raw events are read from the database in pages of 1,000.
ReadingFile: Reading the file (static analysis, in a separate process)…
ReportMissingBody: This analysis is no longer in History.
ReportsSubtitle: Compare two analyses and find exported reports.
ReputationPrivacy: Only the SHA-256 hash is sent, and only to services you enabled in Settings. The file never leaves this computer.
ResetBody: All settings return to their defaults. Your analyses are kept.
RulePacksHelp: Write your own rules as JSON (no code). Put .json files in the rules folder; IDs must start with USR-.
RulesSummary: {0} built-in rules, {1} from your rule packs
RunControlsHelp: You can also use the sandbox window yourself: click through installers, open files.
RunExtended: The run was extended by 2 minutes
RunFinishing: Finishing the run and collecting results
SameSampleNote: Both analyses are of the same file (same SHA-256).
SecretsWeak: On this system keys are only obfuscated, not encrypted. Prefer Windows, where they are protected for your account.
SecuritySubtitle: Is the analysis environment itself ready and isolated?
SetAccentHelp: All three come from the Blazma family palette. Used for buttons and selection only; risk levels always keep their own colours.
SetAiBody: Optional explanations from an AI model running on this computer (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp). It receives the structured report with names and paths removed, never the file. Its answers are labelled as AI and may be wrong; the rule-based answers stay the reference.
SetAiEnableHelp: Adds an AI answer under Ask Blazma's own answer.
SetAiRemote: Allow a server on another computer
SetAiRemoteHelp: Off: only this computer (127.0.0.1, localhost) is accepted. Turn on only for a server you control.
SetAllowlistHelp: One process name or path prefix per line (wildcards allowed). Matching events are hidden; the sample itself is never hidden.
SetDashboardHelp: Choose which cards appear on the dashboard.
SetDefaultEnvironmentHelp: Where new analyses run. Windows Sandbox needs Windows Pro or higher; VirtualBox also works on Windows Home.
SetDemoProvider: Use the demo environment by default
SetDemoProviderHelp: For trying Blazma without Windows Sandbox. Produces synthetic data and labels every result DEMO.
SetHeartbeatHelp: After this long without a heartbeat, monitoring is reported as interrupted.
SetIsolationInfo: The isolation settings are fixed to their safest values.
SetLanguageHelp: Arabic switches the whole interface to right-to-left. Technical terms such as SHA-256, PID, IP and Registry stay as they are.
SetLogLevelHelp: Structured logs never contain file contents or secrets. Applies after restart.
SetLookupAutoHelp: Check the hash as soon as a file is opened. Off: only when you press Check online.
SetLookupPrivacy: Off by default. When enabled, Blazma sends only the file's SHA-256 hash to the services below, never the file, its name or anything else. Each service needs your own free API key.
SetMalwareBazaarHelp: A public collection of known malware samples. A match means the file is already known as malware.
SetMaxEventsHelp: Extra events are counted but not stored.
SetMemoryHelp: RAM given to each Windows Sandbox.
SetNetworkBody: Every analysis starts with networking disabled inside the sandbox. DNS lookups are still recorded, which shows where a program tried to go. You can allow internet access for a single analysis on the New Analysis screen, after a warning.
SetNoTls: Blazma does not intercept or decrypt TLS traffic.
SetNoiseHelp: Hide Windows activity that is not part of the sample's process tree. Persistence changes are always kept.
SetPrivacyFacts: Blazma never uploads files, never sends hashes, and collects no telemetry. Any future cloud feature will be opt-in and clearly labelled.
SetQuotaHelp: Maximum data the sandbox may write back per analysis.
SetRedactHelp: Replace the user name, machine name and profile path in exported reports.
SetReducedMotionHelp: Turns off transitions and the animated score.
SetRelativeTimeHelp: Show time since the sample started (00:01.704) instead of the clock time.
SetRequireDisconnectedHelp: The analysis will not start while the virtual machine has a network adapter attached, unless you enable the real internet for that analysis.
SetRulePacksHelp: JSON rules from your rules folder.
SetShortcutsHelp: Use the format Ctrl+Shift+K. Changes apply immediately.
SetStopTree: Stop early when the program exits
SetStopTreeHelp: End the analysis 10 seconds after the sample and all its child processes have exited.
SetThemeHelp: Dark is the Blazma identity. Midnight and Light follow the rest of the Blazma family.
SetThresholdsHelp: The score at which each verdict starts. Lower values make Blazma stricter.
SetTrustedPublishersHelp: One publisher per line. Recorded for context; it never lowers a score on its own.
SetVirusTotalHelp: Detections from many antivirus engines and a suggested family name.
SetVmHeadlessHelp: Interactive analyses always show the window.
SetVmHelp: Prepare a Windows virtual machine once, with a clean snapshot and no network adapter attached. Every analysis restores that snapshot before and after. See docs/VIRTUAL-MACHINES.md.
SignatureUnverified: Signature present, not verified on this platform
SimulateUserHelp: Moves the mouse and presses Next, I agree and Install. Some programs wait for this before doing anything. Never presses Cancel or Uninstall.
StartNote: The sample runs only inside the selected environment, never on this computer.
StaticNeverRuns: Static analysis reads the file only; it never executes it.
StorageNotWritable: The data folder is not writable
SystemNotReady: Some requirements are missing (see above). You can still explore Blazma with the demo analysis.
SystemReady: System ready. You can analyze files.
ThresholdsInvalid: Thresholds must increase: Suspicious < High < Critical ≤ 100.
TryDemoTip: Runs a synthetic analysis. Nothing is executed.
WatchlistHelp: Add hashes, domains, IPs, paths or process names you want flagged in every analysis. Wildcards * and ? are supported.
WelcomeBody: Give Blazma a file. It inspects it, runs it in an isolated Windows Sandbox, watches what it does, and explains the result: what happened, why it matters, and the evidence.
WelcomeSafety: Blazma is for defensive analysis and authorized security research. Everything stays on this computer.
